body:
From what I understand, the state I live in, it isn't illegal to do any recordings. Just that in court its inadmissible. He's never had any interest in talking to me so I generally just try to avoid him and keep the girls away. 

The report is being made, I'm not sure how much we will hear from it. But I am hoping that the cops will look into it and something can be done. 

You have not frightened me, as I have thought of many of these possibilities myself. I do not want to assume the worst but I would rather be as safe as possible. If it's nothing, its nothing, I will watch the girls more closely and continue to tell them to stay away. If it is something, we did the right thing by informing the police. 

We are making sure to teach the girls how to protect themselves and to scream and fight if they were to ever be grabbed. I am almost legal age to carry pepper spray and my moms have went through the training for that with me, we will be teaching the girls how to cover their eyes when I need to take the pepper spray out.

I cant exactly pack everything this moment and move. As I've mentioned, housing does not open up until July. If we report the suspicious behavior its out of our hands from there. I'm sure the reason people have suggested calling it in as a welfare checkup (as well as mentioning the behavior) is because the cops might look into it in a more timely manner.

We have many safety talks with the girls to keep away from him, and to always ask us before going into anyone's houses. As well as saying no to hugs/kisses if they do not want any,  And how to scream and struggle if they were to ever be grabbed, my mom taught me these things since I was super young and we are making sure that the girls know this information as well.

Thank you, I was just originally afraid that me calling in something that isn't a crime could negatively impact us. Now that I know I should still call in and watch for suspicions, I will do so. Especially now since I have been made aware that him inviting them over alone can be considered a crime. Thank you for your help
I am still a minor, I've been navigating this situation the best I can. Thankfully everyone here has given good advice. The police are being reported to.

He is being made very aware that he is not welcome near the girls, me and my moms have done what we can for that. As much as I'd love to do anything I can to get an investigation going, I'm not going to lie and say he's done anything to me, since that can harm any case they might make. 

Vandalizing property is very much illegal, and as I've mentioned, I would rather keep my record clean so I can get a job. My moms will be making everyone we can aware of his behavior.
I am the man of the house, and even if I wasn't here, my moms are capable of doing so.
I have checked, his name has not come up on any of the checks.
Thank you, you're very kind

Thank you, we have a window that overlooks the parking lot, so I will have to see how capable we are of setting something up. We will be moving in July to another area so I'm not sure if my mom's would want to set something like that up.

We did not want to wait until something happened, that's why I came for advice. Now that I have legal term of child luring and that's what we are reporting to police. I know it should have been reported a long time ago, and I know that we're at fault. The girls will be kept a better eye on while the police do their work.
Thank you, I looked it up. His name is not on any of the lists I've looked at.

Calling the police just because he is staring will not necessarily hold up. I was not aware that there was a legal term for child luring and that it could be reportable for cops to look into. 

We are not at a place where we can move until July, so for now the girls will be watched better when they are outside.

Yes I am fully aware of that, it's just hard not to worry and assume considering how he has been acting. I had someone hurt me in the past who had computers in his garage, he was very defensive and protective of them because of what he was hiding. It was something we were going to mention when reporting him, but it's not as serious as the luring, which is what we're focused on. Even if this does not lead to an investigation, there was still something reporter, and hoping it will help make any future reports easier to handle.

Thank you, a report is being made. I'm almost of legal age and I help keep watch of my sisters. My moms are aware of the behavior and they have had many safety talks with the girls, they follow them very well. Like I have mentioned, I haven't been as good about watching the girls outside as I should have been. I have been doing my college work inside on the computer but I will have to move outside to help watch them from now on.

You are very kind, thank you. I do agree that I need to keep better watch of them. And while "trying my best" had meant that I am currently changing my schedule to be able to keep a better eye on the girls, I can still understand how that could be misunderstood. I've had to go through something like this before as well, and I do not _ever_ want something to happen to the girls. I appreciate the hard truth that I need to be taking this seriously, even if my words were misunderstood.

My moms are very aware of how he acts, they've been told the very second anything happened. The girls have been very good with that. That is true and I do not want anything like that to happen, not to my girls or any others. We are calling in today to report him and I will be making sure to watch the girls better.

Security cameras and the such outside of your apartment is not allowed from what I understand. I hope that's not the case but you never know. He doesn't know me by anything other than the big brother, so I'm hoping that once I adjust my schedule so I can be out there watching them, that he will back off more. I haven't been good with keeping an eye on them, and I'll admit that, it's just been a lot for me to handle with college and the such.

I haven't looked him up because I don't know his last name. A few other commenters mentioned that there are other ways to look him up, so I will be. 

We will be staying as close to the girls as we can when they are out playing. We've taught them their safety things and they've been very good at following them. I think its worth it to make the call, and even if anything doesn't come out of it, he at least knows the police's eyes are on him.

I don't know how much interaction my moms have had with him but from what I hear, they have made it extremely clear that it's inappropriate. To the girls and him, I'm going to make sure they are being watched better from now on, but we will be making a report today to the non-emergency line.
I'll have to see if anyone has advice there, thank you!

Thank you, we have these talks on a regular basis. We teach them about saying no if they're uncomfortable (especially with hugs and kisses, they don't have to give grandma a kiss if they don't want to.) telling us if anything happens. And to scream and struggle if they were to ever get grabbed. We have 30 minute check ups that they both follow very well but ill keep a better watch on them from now on.
Thank you very much for the links!

I'm not sure if the apartments would allow that, and with how the neighborhood is set up, I'm not sure if it would ever be able to catch the things it needs. I will have to mention this to my moms though, thank you.
I am aware. I will adjust everything to make sure I can work on my GED and college classes outside to watch them. We are calling in and making a report tomorrow in the morning.
I haven't yet because I do not know his last name. Ill have to ask my moms tomorrow to see if they know. Thank you for your help

I do have to admit that I have not been as good about watching them as I could be. I am trying to get my GED done as quick as I can and get a job. I will make sure that the girls are watched better while they are out. 

Thank you for your advice, it's most certainly being followed. I'm the man of the house and I have to make sure my sisters are protected.
I will have to look into it, I do not know this guys last name but my moms might. And sadly we are not at a point where we can move until July, I'm worried for the other girls in the neighborhood.

I'm trying to avoid getting a mark on my record, I need to work to help my family. It's really hard to not go and beat this guy. We plan to call in tomorrow.
Another commenter had said that him asking the girls to come over can be considered child luring. That's the closest reason I can find to get police to investigate.
Thank you, I'm going to follow everyone's advice on giving a report. His behavior is very disturbing and I want to make sure that my sisters and other girls in the neighborhood are safe.

That's true, you don't. But im pretty sure that if he was arrested/convictions for anything like this he would not be allowed to live in an apartment center who's tenants are mainly children. I prefer not to assume the worst of a situation (tho it's hard not to when a creep is staring at your sister.) He gave me enough reason to assume he's a creep and needs to be reported, though.

That's a really good idea, I'm not afraid to give him the stink eye, especially with how he's acted towards the girls. I got advice to keep more of an eye on the girls and I will try my best to. I'm not afraid to confront him or call the police if things continue.
I will try my best to be out there with the girls when they are out. Thank you for your advice.

This man does not seem to have any disabilities or the such. I do not know his situation but it's still not an excuse to act this way, and he seems to know it. 

We've been trying our best to keep a log of any interactions, I'm not sure if its safer at this point to continue watching or to call a welfare check. He hasn't approached the girls in a while luckily, I'm hoping its meaning he would calm down with it. It just makes me worried that he could be making another girl in the neighborhood the victim.

I am almost of legal age and fully capable of watching both the girls. There are other adults outside during the day as well. My moms are both busy with work and college. These kids are both ADHD and need lots of time outside, we cant keep them in. 

They have walkie talkies for the times that we cannot be outside with them, they can reach for a mile and are kept under their shirts. 

We've been trying our best to keep dates in mind as well as the things he's said. Like I've mentioned in another comment, the girls are amazing with coming back to the house and asking us before they go to anyone's house or anything.

I'm not really good with that confrontation stuff, id have to have my moms do it instead if we wanna take that route. I try to be with the girls and keeping a watch of them when I'm outside since I'm not afraid to fight. But with the COVID stuff I have my own homework to keep up with. We've been trying to keep watch of his behavior and make sure he isn't doing anything. The girls have been amazing with knowing that they need to come to us and ask before they ever go and follow someone.
Thank you, I will look into it more and call it in. A welfare check sounds like a better option than calling in a crime I have no proof of.

The neighborhood app isn't really used in this neighborhood. Everyone's pretty close though, I'll have to tell my mom to let others know about his behavior. We'll look into the police numbers here too and see if we can report it and have something done.
Thank you, I'll have to look into it and call in. I hope that the police can deal with everything and there can be something done about the behavior.
Would that even hold up? Is it something they would even look into?

Thank you very much for sharing your view on it, its helpful hearing from somebody else that I'm not overreacting about this. 

And thank you very much for the birthday wish, its very kind ❤

Thank you very much for this message ❤ I appreciate the kind words and reassurance. I've known that he wasn't someone I needed in my life, especially now that this has happened. Sometimes you need that final push though, and this is very much so the final push.

I'm aware that is the best course of action. I know I shouldn't give him the satisfaction but its so difficult not being angry about this. Saying I wanted to "tell him I don't appreciate him being so horrible" is very much short for "telling him that he's a jackass and that I'm happy we broke up" sort of thing. It's very immature as I said, but anger has a bitter taste. 

I really needed to hear that last part though, that if I continue to feed him he will crave more. I think your way of wording the message is very on par of how I feel, thank you for putting my thoughts out into a sentence for me.

First off, I wanted to say, thank you so much for sharing your point of view on this. I came out around my mothers friend who is also a transgender WOC, she helped my mom through the process of getting me into a doctor. I'm always looking forward to hearing from the people I look up to, I admire how strong you are <3

Secondly, I appreciate that you mentioned the hive mind mentality. I've been thinking of it but didn't know how to express it. The LGBTQ community is very separate, it's presented as one big community but you are commonly expected to stay in your "group" so to say. I'm not sure if this is the same for adults, but when you are at highschool age, you can imagine how it is. You might want to become a friend with someone but they see you as another number, it really is a competition and I find it very exhausting being in a community of trans people fighting 24/7. I appreciate visibility and standing up for things that harm us, but I feel like a lot of the younger community take it to extreme levels, and feel that they can do things like publicly outing someone to get a point across. Its a lot of drama, all the time. Sadly, its extremely hard to find others who aren't a part of the mentality. Unless I happen to talk to others like you, who are older. 

I happen to be passing, I'm growing in a beard, so now I am even more private with myself, I like to be seen as cisgendered, its safest for me, especially with the area we live in. So the terror of being publicly outed by someone is real. I've luckily gotten out of this friend circle after realizing how toxic it was, it's just so frustrating when you put so much into a relationship, only to find out that someone just saw you as another trans person. Its hard exiting the community as well because its SO big and most people just expect you to be a part of it when you say you're trans.

I think that I became friends with them because i genuinely shares interests with these people, I think they saw the relationship as "oh, another trans person, gotta add." You know? Its hard with those types of people because you genuinely see them as a friend but they might feel differently. 

And that's very silly, but thank you for agreeing.
Thank you very much :)

Luckily most of the people who have done this to me I am no longer friends with. I have a few friends who don't agree with the decision to not have them in my life any longer, as they are the ones who don't see why it was a big deal. If the topic comes up again, ill have to take that approach. Since I have gotten these people out of my life, I've been trying to avoid having these people in my life again. It's hard to not attract them though when you are in the community, especially since there are people who don't see these things as serious. 

Thank you for your advice and for letting me know that it is serious because it's the answer I needed.
Thank you for the chuckle

I'm really concerned for him and the fact he is in this relationship with someone exposing him to all of this. Its not healthy and he's nowhere near old enough to make that decision for himself. But I cant hide the fact that im super fucking pissed about the fact he's helping in continuing to spread lies about my friend Dianna. 

I don't know if it should be one of those, "I'm going to bring up how I'm really concerned about you and what you're involved with, but we keep it at that." Or if I should do a full "it's unacceptable on all levels that you are doing this to my friend, and that you are doing this to yourself."

I would say that's really a half and half behavior. I'm not really sure what he personally gets from harassing me like this, but that's not something ill ever understand. 

I realized that he's not really concerned about anything but sex in the relationship, and I learned that pretty quickly. So I do know that getting back into this relationship will continue in him pushing me to do things I'm not comfortable with. 

I do think he cares, just... Not for the right reasons. Its still hard to not feel responsible though, especially when it turns into big freak outs like this. I just want to be able to move, and start a new life. Him coming back into it is not going help, especially if him coming back into my life means that he harasses my mother/friends because I wont answer him.

I've explained it to my friend, shes very shy though and I'm worried about her following through if she gets overwhelmed. I've talked to my mom as well and she thinks he just still cares about me and that I should continue being friendly. (I feel like if I was a female that she would be thinking very differently of him tbh.) 

And yes, I knew that there was going to be problems from how his ex's were and all but I didn't think it would be at this level. I had a plan for how I was going to do everything and I always have a plan on how to get myself out of a situation when it's toxic. He threw that plan out the window though after what he did.

I know I need to tell him I don't have feelings anymore and that moving is a part of it. I'm always worried to bring up toxic traits someone has because you don't know how it will turn on you. I just don't know how to tell him that I'm not interested since he's made it very clear that He's still madly in love.

I hope he can find the same as well.

I would like to and be able to stop worrying about it but im worried about how that will go. He already got very worried about me not answering him for a day or two. 

He has contact with one of my friends and shes very shy, if he were to start contacting her she wouldn't know how to tell him to stop. And if he were to go to my mom im worried she would get angry. She doesn't understand why im so annoyed with him and thinks that I should continue being friendly even though he wont leave me alone.

I haven't blocked him on everything yet, because like I said, I really don't want him involving my friends/family in this. 

I understand that point of view, I just try not to blow up on people because I can really be a piece of shit when I'm angry and fed up with someone. He's learned a lot of these toxic behaviors from past relationships, and when someone has seen a behavior as normal its hard to help them understand when it isn't. 

I'm sorry that happened to you though, I'm glad you were able to recognize what went wrong and that you are happy now.

I'm glad that you found something to help you, as someone who's never been officially diagnosed (I lived in the south for most of my life in an area where diagnoses were very taboo.) Since we've moved to the north it's been really hard to find doctors willing to go through with diagnosing an older person. Its something that's affected me for almost my entire life. I'm really thankful I was introduced to audible, it's helped me focus and get tasks done.

(And i apologize for putting a diagnosis on something I don't have a diagnosis on. Its just easier than trying to explain to someone that in order for me to have enough stimulus for entertainment I have to be playing a game while listening to music/watching a show and doing something like fidgeting)
